sentences.text: Leidyosuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodilian from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, classified as either an alligatoroid or a stem-group crocodilian.
It is considered one of the most basal members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.
In 2026, researchers described the morphology of the endocranial structures of Leidyosuchus canadensis.
The genus was named in 1907 by Lawrence Lambe, with L. canadensis designated as the type species.
There are 47 recorded fossil occurrences of Leidyosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
Fossils of Leidyosuchus are known from the middle Campanian age Dinosaur Park Formation.
The time range for Leidyosuchus is estimated from the Santonian to the Danian, spanning 85.7 to 63.4 million years ago.

A 2025 study by Jules D. Walter and colleagues argues that Leidyosuchus may not be a true alligatoroid or even a true crocodilian, but rather a derived non-crocodilian eusuchian that split from the lineage leading to Crocodilia before Deinosuchus.
